interpretation: Of things moved per se, some are moved by nature and some by force and contrary to nature (254b12-24); the closing summary takes this as exhaustive of everything moved (255b31: εἰ δὴ πάντα τὰ κινούμενα ἢ φύσει κινεῖται ἢ παρὰ φύσιν καὶ βίᾳ). Read as a division of each motion of a thing in a respect. The 'if' (εἰ δή) introduces the summary's premises, which Aristotle has argued in the chapter; it is not a hypothesis he leaves open. Per accidens motion (254b7-12) is set aside before the division; the reading quantifies over all motions, which is the summary's own scope. Scope: physical motion only (`IsPhysicalRespect`: place, quality, quantity), the motion the Physics treats; the reading says nothing about other reductions from potency to act. `MovedIn` here is being moved per se; per accidens being moved (the sailor carried by the ship, 254b7-12) is not a separate predicate and is set aside, as the division sets it aside.
